title: Inside KC Ghost Hunters: The team investigating paranormal activity across the metro
excerpt: There are people in this world who get in their car after work, head home and spend the rest of their evening unwinding on the couch or staring at their phones.
content:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- There are people in this world who get in their car after work, head home and spend the rest of their evening unwinding on the couch or staring at their phones.

Others grab their friends, some equipment and a whole lot of courage to pursue a hobby that deals with the unconventional, the unorthodox and the potentially paranormal.

Jaden Deason wakes up every morning and heads to his 9-to-5 at a local warehouse. But even though it pays the bills, it isn't where his passions lie.

 'I am Andre Dettonville': A centuries-old ghost story tied to the Linda Hall Library 

That is reserved for after work, when he and four other supernatural enthusiasts gather together to embark on their next investigation.

The team is called the KC Ghost Hunters, and Deason is the founder. Each member brings their own unique skill set, experience and perspectives to the group. But more importantly, they all have a mission of "going where the lights flicker," so others don't have to.

Jakob Groom is an artist, mechanic and musician, but works as a part-time investigator on the team. Andrew Lower is a full-time high school special education teacher and the medium of the group. Devin Plasm is a videographer and uses his talent to capture the investigations, as well as the moments that cannot be explained.

They have been investigating since 2024. Deason had just graduated from college with a degree in parapsychology when he decided to create KC Ghost Hunters. But the origins of the group go back even further.

For Deason and most of the crew, the fascination with the paranormal world began in childhood, with each of them recalling paranormal encounters, unexplained apparitions or other obscure experiences from their past.

According to the group, this common thread is what ultimately led them to each other.

"I grew up in a home here in Grain Valley that had kind of a lot of activity. We were seeing orbs and all that stuff...I think I put a thing out on social media. I was like, 'Hey, who'd want to go ghost hunting?' And then that's how I got Jakob," Deason said.

"Andrew had actually messaged the Facebook page at some point and was like, 'Hey, I would love to go along with you guys on a visit.' And then we went on a ghost hunt."

Just a few days before joining, Lower had actually met with Deason to help him cleanse his house. Deason said he was fearful he had "brought something home" after hearing footsteps and things moving around. So, Lower came in and helped him resolve the problem.

"I was like, 'Hey, this guy's the real deal,'" Deason said. "And now he's with us."

The group isn't just a ragtag team of strangers who met online, though. Deason and Groom have known each other since high school and stayed in touch over the years before reconnecting for this common mission – a mission that has now turned into a real-life side hustle and aspirational full-time gig.

But what does KC Ghost Hunters actually do? And, to speak for all the skeptics out there, what have they seen, and how can they prove it?

Investigations and Paranormal Encounters

From historic properties to private family homes, KC Ghost Hunters has investigated multiple places across the Kansas City metro.

When asked which locations stand out as the scariest or most memorable among their investigations, the group immediately went to a well-known property with years of ghost stories attached to it.

The Rice-Tremonti home, located in Raytown, was built in 1844. The Gothic Revival structure sits on six acres alongside the Santa Fe Trail and is known as the oldest standing frame house in Jackson County.

But for the last 182 years, it has welcomed not just cobwebs and renovations, but also endless rumors surrounding the paranormal.

"We went to the Rice-Tremonti home, and we're going back again this year," Deason said.

The group arrived at the historic property to investigate its alleged hauntings. At some point in the evening, they did what they usually do: started a séance.

They closed every door, turned the lights off and sat at the dining room table surrounded by a ring of salt. Before they knew it, things started getting strange.

"We were talking to multiple entities there, and all of a sudden, Andrew and I looked to the right, and we saw footprints under the door right next to us, and there was nobody there. Every single person in the building was in that dining room, surrounded by salt and closed in our séance circle," Deason said.

"As soon as we brought it up, we watched those footsteps walk away from the door, and it was very creepy."

He also recalled a glass lantern falling to the ground amid the chaos, and each member of the group agreed there was no logical way that could have happened.

"It was in the center of the hardwood table," Deason said. "Those are pretty heavy. They don't just fall."

When asked whether this was caught on camera, the group looked at each other and collectively sighed.

"We have footage directly after, but our camera... our camera, I know, it's awful," Deason said. "It's awful because sometimes, things will happen not on camera. And it's like, like purposely whatever is there, whatever we're dealing with, it's gotta be smarter."

They went on to say that some things never manage to get captured on camera, but sometimes they are lucky.

In fact, KC Ghost Hunters managed to keep the camera rolling at one of their recent private home investigations – leading them to create a 42-minute YouTube video documenting the experience.

The home sits in the rural river town of Lexington, Missouri, located in Lafayette County. The owners reached out to the group for guidance after experiencing some unexplained phenomena in different parts of their home.

From shadows appearing in the background of family photos to the owners feeling like someone is watching them to family pets barking at random corners, the property checked many of the KC Ghost Hunters' boxes and prompted them to launch the investigation.

"We had lots of activity. We had all of our sensors being tripped," Lawson said, describing the experience. "A lot of us felt like we were being touched by things."

"Some people living in the home were experiencing things, as well. It was kind of a wild time because I think one of the things that was said on the AM-FM was there's a portal."

Lawson added, "So, I think we're dealing with multiple entities. And it was like, one point, it was like, okay, this is getting a little bit too freaky even for me."

Eventually, the group completed their investigation and determined that one of the entities was the homeowner's father, who was simply watching over the family to make sure they were safe.

But to prove the theory further, Groom said they decided to scan a photo of the father that was hanging on the wall to see if any energy was detected. Their theory proved correct.

"There was something standing next to the photo," Groom recalled, "And I said, you know what? If I was a ghost, and if I was here and there was a picture of me on the wall, I would say, 'Hey guys, this is me. I'm right here.'"

Protections before, during and after an investigation

After many hours on the property, the family was able to get some answers before the group severed their ties with the spirits inside the house and left. But it turns out the effects of an investigation can linger even after it wraps up.

"We were all exhausted," Groom said. "I ended up feeling sick about the time that I got home, and just nauseous. Very nauseous."

"I ended up laying down in the clothes that I had investigated in, and then I woke up, changed, went back to sleep, and then I woke up the next morning drenched in sweat like I had broke a fever. So, I was sick for about like eight hours. I took a shower and immediately felt better."

Groom later attributed the spontaneous illness to an experiment he tried earlier that day. He recalled wanting to see what would happen if he didn't take the precautionary measures he usually takes before an investigation.

Before walking into many of these homes, crew members of KC Ghost Hunters usually protect themselves before, during and after interacting with spirits.

According to Plasm, they often use spiritual cleansing items, like holy water, sage and salts to ensure they are protected before and after they leave. But the resident medium of the group, Lawson, stated he sometimes takes extra precautions by performing various rituals with the team.

"So I do the LBRP, which is a banishing ritual, and also do either a prayer or a good kind of vibes and things," Lawson said.

He added that sometimes a clapping ritual, white candles and obsidian are used to ensure they leave them alone. They also frequently import a "paranormal protection kit" from France for protection during their private home investigations.

Some of these items are also used to banish spirits; however, to cast a spirit out of a home depends largely on the place, the spirit and the people living on the property.

According to Deason, they will never banish anything at a historic home. As for private homes, it simply comes down to the owners' requests.

In the case of their last investigation, the homeowners wanted the spirits to be cast out. And based on their reaction, it seems like the KC Ghost Hunters crew did their jobs successfully.

"They were satisfied customers. They were very happy," Groom said, before Deason added that the homeowners claimed the house "felt lighter."

According to the crew, nothing feels better than being able to help families find peace and comfort in and outside of their homes. "We'll get messages where it's like, 'Oh, we can't thank you enough for what happened,'" Deason said, further emphasizing that this is exactly why they do what they do.

"Any questions you have, just please feel free to reach out and talk to us, and we'll give you every knowledgeable piece that we have," he concluded.

The KC Ghost Hunters have another investigation this November. To watch their most recent home investigation, go to their YouTube channel, "KC Ghost Hunters," to see how the experience unfolds.
